items.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: I went to Birdland to hear Bud Powell play. That was it for me.

ctx.x: That’s great. Did you feel a need at a certain age to, you mentioned getting out of Indianapolis. Time to spread your own wings a little bit?

Well see when we played the Apollo Theater we had such success that the booking agents wanted us to stay in New York. And we would have had a good success in New York. But my sisters wanted to go back to Indianapolis. You know how ladies are. And so we didn’t stay. And after I was in New York the first time I remember when I was there I went to Birdland to hear Bud Powell play. That was it for me. I had to come to New York after that. And that’s all I talked about from that time until I got to New York is I have…
So you took the long way. Did you have your first arrangement played with him? With Buddy Johnson?

items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: My brother took me to Birdland. Bud Powell was playing. It was so fantastic. The impression that it left with me was so incredible...

ctx.x: The Armory or something like that.

They’d play in a convention center, with no microphones, and you could hear everything. It was a good lesson for us, because we hadn’t had the opportunity to play opposite with a band like that. We played opposite Louis Jordan with his quintet and things like that, which was really wonderful too. But that was my first chance to go to New York. I had the opportunity to go to Birdland. My brother took me to Birdland. Bud Powell was playing. It was so fantastic. The impression that it left with me was so incredible…
Were you already thinking about bebop at that point?
